entries.risk_mechanism: Obligation can be weakened, strengthened, or confused with description.
entries.contextual_requirements: Compare the governing verb, subject, and exception; present tense may itself impose an obligation in legislative French.
entries.limitations: Lexical presence is only a routing cue; it is not an equivalence judgment.

entries.risk_mechanism: Permission or discretion may be rendered as duty or mere possibility.
entries.contextual_requirements: Inspect legal actor, scope, and whether the construction is permissive or epistemic.

entries.risk_mechanism: Dropped, inserted, or scope-shifted negation reverses propositional content.
entries.contextual_requirements: Check discontinuous French negation and the full syntactic scope.
entries.limitations: Negative-looking morphology and idioms can be non-compositional.

entries.risk_mechanism: Condition, exception, or trigger can disappear or attach to the wrong rule.
entries.contextual_requirements: Resolve clause boundary and distinguish temporal from conditional readings.

entries.risk_mechanism: A changed anchor, unit, inclusivity rule, or duration changes legal timeliness.
entries.contextual_requirements: Read the number, unit, start event, and inclusive/exclusive wording together.
entries.limitations: This cue does not calculate calendars or jurisdictional deadline rules.

entries.risk_mechanism: Digits, units, bounds, ranges, or decimal conventions can change factual or legal effect.
entries.contextual_requirements: Compare sign, value, unit, range operator, and locale-specific separators.
entries.limitations: Every digit is routed, so dates and identifiers may be false positives.

entries.risk_mechanism: Quantifier or list scope can expand or narrow the affected class.
entries.contextual_requirements: Inspect coordination, list boundaries, and the noun phrase governed.

entries.risk_mechanism: An exception or reservation can be omitted or applied to the wrong proposition.
entries.contextual_requirements: Locate the governed provision and any cross-reference.
entries.limitations: Cross-document references are outside this lexical router.

entries.risk_mechanism: A short connective may be omitted yet alter alternatives, conjunction, contrast, or consequence.
entries.contextual_requirements: Compare coordinated constituents and discourse relation, not isolated words.
entries.limitations: High-frequency words intentionally trade precision for recall.

entries.risk_mechanism: Near-synonymous institutional terms can name a different competent body.
entries.contextual_requirements: Confirm the official institutional identity in current authoritative terminology.
entries.limitations: Not a copied termbase; the short list is independently authored and incomplete.
entries.reuse_rights: independently authored CC0-1.0; TERMDAT rights not asserted

entries.risk_mechanism: A procedural remedy, decision, or application term may be mapped to a different legal act.
entries.contextual_requirements: Use domain, authority, and procedural stage; consult authoritative terminology manually.
entries.limitations: Deliberately small and not suitable as a legal dictionary.
entries.reuse_rights: independently authored CC0-1.0; TERMDAT rights not asserted

entries.risk_mechanism: Similar orthography can conceal different meanings or modality.
entries.contextual_requirements: Require contextual semantic comparison; never flag similarity alone as an error.
entries.limitations: Patterns are independent examples, not extracted from the cited resource; senses vary by context.
entries.reuse_rights: independently authored CC0-1.0; cited resource MIT
